title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion
credits: Photos: Alexander Shatov, Mariia Berezovsky, Solen Feyissa, Timothy Hales Bennett / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Facebook's owner, Meta, has been ordered to pay twenty-five billion dollars, to a single American state.
On Wednesday, Judge Francis Mathew in New Mexico set the penalty, after a jury found Meta had misled Facebook users.
In September, jurors found more than forty-three million violations of New Mexico's consumer protection laws.
The case goes back to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
A personality quiz app harvested data from about eighty-seven million Facebook profiles, and that data went to Cambridge Analytica.
The firm's clients included Donald Trump's twenty sixteen election campaign.
New Mexico had asked for thirty-five to forty billion dollars. Meta argued for no more than three point four billion.
The judge said Facebook's wrongdoing goes to the heart of its core business practices.
Attorney General Raúl Torrez called it one of the largest, if not the largest, state verdicts against a company in American history.
By law, the money would go to education in New Mexico, but Meta has said it plans to appeal.
And Meta's shares still rose about two percent after the news.
